name: Project Closeout Checklist
description: A step-by-step guide to closing a project cleanly and capturing what you learned.

items.text: Confirm every deliverable is complete against the scope
Run a final quality check on each output
Resolve any outstanding defects or punch-list items
Hand over final files in the agreed formats
Verify the client or sponsor can access everything
items.note: Test access links before declaring delivery done.

items.text: Compare results against the original success criteria
Walk the sponsor or client through the final deliverables
Obtain written acceptance and sign-off
Close out any open change requests
Confirm there are no disputed items remaining
Reconcile the final budget against actual spending
Submit and confirm payment of all invoices
Close purchase orders and vendor contracts
Cancel or transfer any recurring subscriptions
Record the final cost for future estimates
items.note: Accurate actuals improve the next project's budget.

items.text: Gather feedback from the team and stakeholders
List what went well and should be repeated
List what went wrong and how to avoid it
Review actual performance against the plan
Document recommendations for future projects
items.note: Store lessons where the next team will actually find them.

items.text: Collect all final documents, files, and reports
Organize and label files in a shared archive
Back up critical data in a secure location
Update any registers, asset lists, or records
Note who owns the archive going forward
Release team members back to other work
Recover or reassign equipment and licenses
Revoke access that is no longer needed
items.note: Removing stale access reduces security risk.

items.text: Thank the team and recognize their contributions
Send a final closure note to stakeholders
Formally mark the project as closed

faq.a: It is the final phase where you confirm all work is complete, get sign-off, settle accounts, archive records, and release resources. A proper closeout ends the project cleanly.

faq.q: Why is a closeout checklist important?
faq.a: It stops loose ends like unpaid invoices, unowned files, and unrecorded lessons. It also creates a clear record that the project met its goals and was formally accepted.
A short session where the team discusses what went well and what to improve. Documenting it turns one project's experience into better results on the next.

faq.q: When should I start project closeout?
faq.a: Begin as the final deliverables near completion, not after everyone has moved on. Starting early makes it easier to gather sign-off, feedback, and documentation while people are still engaged.

faq.q: Can I print this project closeout checklist?
faq.a: Yes. Download the printable PDF, share it with your team, and check off each task as you finalize deliverables, sign-off, archiving, and resource release.
